_meta.indication: Indicated to delay the onset of Stage 3 type 1 diabetes in adults and pediatric patients 8 years of age and older with Stage 2 type 1 diabetes.

pivotal_trials.population: Patients 8 to 49 years of age with Stage 2 type 1 diabetes
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time from randomization to development of Stage 3 type 1 diabetes diagnosis
pivotal_trials.result: Median time to Stage 3 T1D diagnosis was 50 months with TZIELD vs 25 months with placebo (difference of 25 months); statistically significant delay with hazard ratio 0.41 (95% CI: 0.22 to 0.78; p=0.0066).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were lymphopenia, rash, leukopenia and headache. Warnings include cytokine release syndrome (5% of TZIELD-treated vs 0.8% control), serious infections (3.5% vs 2%), lymphopenia (78% vs 11%), and hypersensitivity reactions.
target_moa: A CD3-directed humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds CD3 on T lymphocytes; the mechanism may involve partial agonistic signaling and deactivation of pancreatic beta cell autoreactive T lymphocytes and an increase in regulatory T cells.
modality: mAb (CD3-directed humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody)
companion_dx_detail: FDA agreed with the sponsor that the islet cell autoantibody assays used for patient selection are not companion diagnostics.

advisory_committee.vote: EMDAC met on May 27, 2021; ten members voted yes and 7 voted no on whether benefits outweigh risks in support of approval.

description.text: Expanded indication to delay onset of Stage 3 type 1 diabetes to pediatric patients 1 to 8 years of age with Stage 2 T1D

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for updates to the Prescribing Information and Medication Guide based on data from Part A of trial PRV-031-005/SFY18116 entitled, Single Arm, Open-label Study to Assess the Safety and Pharmacokinetics of a 14-day Regimen of Teplizumab in Pediatric Stage 2 Diabetes (Participants With at Least Two Autoantibodies and Dysglycemia), including expansion of the indication to delay the onset of Stage 3 type 1 diabetes (T1D) to pediatric patients between 1 to 8 years of age with Stage 2 T1D.

basis.text: FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation on 8/2/2019 (IND 102629).
The application was a Class 2 resubmission of priority review.

citations.quote: Priority or Standard	Class 2 resubmission of priority review

summary.text: Teplizumab-mzwv received Breakthrough Therapy Designation in 2019 and was reviewed under priority review. The original BLA (submitted October 31, 2020) received a Complete Response on July 2, 2021 over bioequivalence/CMC deficiencies; a Class 2 resubmission received February 17, 2022 was approved November 17, 2022 as a full (non-accelerated) approval based on Study TN-10.

requirement.text: 4359-1: Conduct a 12-month single-arm, open-label study to assess the safety and PK of teplizumab-mzwv in pediatric patients 0 to less than 8 years of age with two T1D-related autoantibodies and dysglycemia (Stage 2 T1D) [Part A], followed by a 12-month open-label extension [Part B].

citations.quote: 4359-1 Conduct a 12-month single-arm, open-label study to assess the safety and pharmacokinetics (PK) of teplizumab-mzwv in pediatric patients 0 to less than 8 years of age with two type-1 diabetes (T1D)-related autoantibodies

requirement.text: 4359-2: Conduct an observational registry study to assess the long-term safety of teplizumab-mzwv in patients with Stage 2 T1D, evaluating CRS, serious infections, hypersensitivity, lymphoproliferative disorders and malignancy, with a comparator group and at least 150 exposed subjects monitored at least 10 years.

citations.quote: 4359-2 Conduct an observational registry study to assess the long-term safety of teplizumab-mzwv in patients with Stage 2 type 1 diabetes.

The study design should include a comparator group and monitor patients for at least 10 years after their first course of treatment. The study should enroll at least 150 subjects exposed to teplizumab-mzwv and collect sufficient clinical information to assess for sources of confounding for the target outcomes.

basis.text: The Office of Clinical Pharmacology recommended withholding approval because of deficiencies related to lack of demonstration of bioequivalence between the to-be-marketed drug product (AGC Biologics) and the clinical study drug product (Eli Lilly), along with CMC and facility deficiencies.
